slot.brief: A nucleus undergoes alpha decay; compute energy released using given binding energies of parent, daughter and alpha, then find kinetic energy of the alpha particle.

stem: A stationary nucleus $^{220}\text{X}$ undergoes $\alpha$-decay into $^{216}\text{Y}$. The total binding energies of $^{220}\text{X}$, $^{216}\text{Y}$, and the $\alpha$-particle are $1700.0\text{ MeV}$, $1677.2\text{ MeV}$, and $28.3\text{ MeV}$, respectively. The kinetic energy of the emitted $\alpha$-particle is

verdicts.working: Q = BE(Y) + BE(α) − BE(X) = 1677.2 + 28.3 − 1700.0 = 5.5 MeV. Momentum conservation splits Q inversely with masses: KE_α = Q·(216/220) = 5.4 MeV (recoil takes 0.1 MeV).

working:
The nuclear disintegration reaction is:
$${}^{220}\text{X} \to {}^{216}\text{Y} + {}^4_2\text{He}$$

The total energy released ($Q$-value) in terms of binding energy (BE) is:
$$Q = \text{BE}({}^{216}\text{Y}) + \text{BE}(\alpha) - \text{BE}({}^{220}\text{X})$$
$$Q = 1677.2\text{ MeV} + 28.3\text{ MeV} - 1700.0\text{ MeV} = 5.5\text{ MeV}$$

Since the parent nucleus is initially at rest, by conservation of linear momentum:
$$p_\alpha = p_Y = p$$

The kinetic energy of each fragment is $K = \dfrac{p^2}{2m}$. Therefore:
$$Q = K_\alpha + K_Y = K_\alpha \left(1 + \dfrac{m_\alpha}{m_Y}\right) = K_\alpha \left(\dfrac{m_Y + m_\alpha}{m_Y}\right)$$

Using masses proportional to mass numbers ($m_Y \approx 216\text{ u}$, $m_\alpha \approx 4\text{ u}$):
$$K_\alpha = \left(\dfrac{A - 4}{A}\right) Q = \left(\dfrac{216}{220}\right) \times 5.5\text{ MeV} = \dfrac{54}{55} \times 5.5\text{ MeV} = 5.4\text{ MeV}$$

Independent check: Q = BE(Y) + BE(α) − BE(X) = 1677.2 + 28.3 − 1700.0 = 5.5 MeV. Momentum conservation splits Q inversely with masses: KE_α = Q·(216/220) = 5.4 MeV (recoil takes 0.1 MeV).

draft.distractor_notes:
A: Uses $K_\alpha = \dfrac{m_\alpha}{m_Y + m_\alpha} Q = \dfrac{4}{220} \times 5.5 = 0.1\text{ MeV}$, which is the kinetic energy of the recoiling daughter nucleus.
B: Uses the elastic collision factor $\dfrac{m_Y - m_\alpha}{m_Y + m_\alpha} Q = \dfrac{212}{220} \times 5.5 = 5.3\text{ MeV}$.
D: Ignores the recoil of the daughter nucleus and assumes the $\alpha$-particle carries all the decay energy ($K_\alpha = Q = 5.5\text{ MeV}$).
